title: Sri Lanka — French strategies and Trincomalee
author_or_institution: Bibliothèque nationale de France — Patrimoines partagés France-Asie du Sud
scope: French East India Company expedition to Trincomalee in 1672, Rajasinghe II, Sun Island, Dutch opposition, Suffren at Trincomalee in 1782 and restitution after European peace.
limitations: Institutional synthesis drawing on French archival and secondary material. Use Cambridge/VOC and naval scholarship to corroborate chronology and strategic mechanism.

title: Introduction — The Company Fortress: Military Engineering and the Dutch East India Company in South Asia, 1638–1795
author_or_institution: Erik Odegard / Amsterdam University Press via Cambridge Core
scope: VOC strategic response in South Asia to the French fleet at Trincomalee in 1672 and the wider Franco-Dutch war; late-eighteenth-century Trincomalee and Ceylon fortification context.
limitations: Military-engineering study; strongest for VOC strategic interpretation and chronology, not for French court policy as a whole.

title: The Van Goens System: Building the Fortifications, 1650–1675
author_or_institution: Erik Odegard / Amsterdam University Press via Cambridge Core
scope: Completion of VOC conquest of Portuguese positions in Ceylon in 1658, Van Goens's fear of Portuguese counter-offensive in 1661, refortification and control of Ceylonese ports.
limitations: Centres the VOC fortification system and Van Goens; it demonstrates that a Portuguese return was still feared but does not by itself explain Lisbon's full post-1658 allocation strategy.

title: Consolidating the Empire (1635–1685) — Wars Overseas
author_or_institution: Gerrit Knaap and Henk den Heijer / Amsterdam University Press via Cambridge Core
scope: VOC offensive against Portuguese positions after 1636, Ceylon within a multi-front Asian war, peace with Portugal ratified in 1663 and consolidation of Dutch imperial power.
limitations: VOC-centred synthesis; should be paired with Portuguese historiography to avoid making Dutch success equivalent to inevitable Portuguese collapse.

title: Looking out from Goa, 1648: Perspectives on a crisis of the Estado da Índia
author_or_institution: Sanjay Subrahmanyam / Modern Asian Studies, Cambridge University Press
scope: Estado da Índia crisis after decades of attacks by VOC and Asian powers, Braganza Restoration in 1640, separation from Spain and institutional reinvention beginning in the 1660s.
limitations: Explains the structural crisis and reinvention of the Portuguese Asian empire; it is not a Ceylon campaign narrative.

title: Renascent Empire? The House of Braganza and the Quest for Stability in Portuguese Monsoon Asia, ca. 1640–1683
author_or_institution: Glenn J. Ames / Amsterdam University Press, Open JSTOR
scope: Portuguese Asian imperial crisis and reform after 1640; Carreira da Índia weakness in 1658–1663; loss of Ceylon and Malacca; stabilization of a reduced Estado by the 1680s.
limitations: Revisionist macro-history of Portuguese Asia. It rejects a simple linear-decline model, so Ceylon's loss must be narrated as one severe contraction within a surviving and reforming Estado.

title: The Politics of Colonial Lists: Conspiracies, Deportations, and Knowledge in 1790s Pondicherry
author_or_institution: Comparative Studies in Society and History / Cambridge University Press
scope: Pondicherry established in 1673; Dutch occupation 1693–1699; repeated British occupations including 1761 and 1793; continuing French political presence in India after 1763.
limitations: The article's main analytical focus is the 1790s, so earlier occupation dates are contextual chronology rather than its central causal argument.

title: The Decisive War (1782–1783) — The British Navy in Eastern Waters
author_or_institution: John D. Grainger / Boydell & Brewer via Cambridge Core
scope: British seizure of Trincomalee in January 1782, Suffren's arrival in the Bay of Bengal with a French squadron and troops, coordination with Haidar Ali and the naval war in eastern waters.
limitations: Naval-war history; use BnF and treaty/colonial chronology for the subsequent restitution of Trincomalee to the Dutch.

title: Port Louis, Isle de France: The Grand Arsenal
author_or_institution: Philip MacDougall / Boydell & Brewer via Cambridge Core
scope: Persistent French naval-commercial infrastructure in the Indian Ocean: Pondicherry, Isle de France/Port Louis and alliances against British expansion.
limitations: Focuses on naval resistance and Port Louis; it should not be used alone to rank French fiscal priorities between Atlantic and Indian Ocean theatres.

title: The French Atlantic World — The Death of the French Atlantic
scope: Long-eighteenth-century French Atlantic empire; late-Ancien-Régime centrality of Caribbean possessions, especially Saint-Domingue, after the colonial wars and 1763 settlement.
limitations: Atlantic context only. It cannot establish that Caribbean profitability directly caused abandonment of Ceylon or French India; Indian Ocean sources show continuing French investment and warfare there.
